对话 1。
Conversation 1.
你好，本杰明。
Hello, Benjamin.
丹和我将去星期六早上沿着运河跑步。
Dan and I will be going for a run along the canal Saturday morning.
你愿意加入我们吗？
Would you like to join us?
我很想去，但我的脚踝受伤了上周末和同事一起踢足球。
I'd love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues.
哦亲爱的。
Oh dear.
严重吗？
Is it serious?
不，一点也不。
No, not at all.
我在摔倒时摔得很重，扭伤了有一点点。
I landed badly during a fall and twisted it a little.
但这没什么大不了的。
But it's no big deal.
只是有点肿，我应该如果你仍然那么我想去慢跑。
It's just a little swollen and I should be fine for next Saturday if you still want to go for a jog then.
下周六我不在这里。
I won't be here next Saturday.
我要去动物园。
I'm going to the zoo.
动物园？
The zoo?
是的，我的小侄子六岁了，他喜欢动物园，所以全家都去。
Yeah, my little nephew turned six and he loves the zoo, so the whole family is going.
哦，那好吧。
Oh, OK then.
自从我还是个孩子。
I haven't been to a zoo since I was a kid.
它们远不如它们受欢迎当我们还是孩子的时候
They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be when we were children.
我个人对可怜的动物感到遗憾被关在笼子里，但不可否认的是对孩子来说既有趣又有教育意义。
I personally feel sorry for the poor animals stuck in cages, but there's no denying they are fun and educational for children.
你知道丹是否会在吗？下周六？
Do you know if Dan will be around next Saturday?
是的，我想他会的。
Yeah, I think he will.
只需给他发一条短信即可。
Just send him a text message.
他一直热衷于体育活动。
He's always keen on physical activities.
这是真的。
That's true.
丹的身体极其健康。
Dan is extremely fit and healthy.
他大多数时间都会去健身房，而且每周打两到三次网球。
He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times a week.
那么，你做了什么来保持脚踝肿了之后很忙吗？
So, what have you been doing to stay busy while you've had that swollen ankle?
我一直在读一些书。
I've been catching up on some reading.
圣诞节我收到了三本书，我现在才有时间读它们。

对话 2。
Conversation 2.
今天书评的嘉宾是约翰布莱克，新畅销书《退休》的作者早期的。
Our guest on today's Book Talk is John Black, the author of the new bestseller, Retire Early.
谢谢你邀请我参加节目，丽莎。
Thanks for having me on the show, Lisa.
约翰，你的书得到了很多注意，部分原因是你写道，大多数人40岁就可以退休。
John, your book is getting a lot of attention, partly because you write that most people can retire by 40.
这现实吗？
Is that realistic?
确实。
Definitely.
在研究这本书的过程中，我采访了数百位40 岁就退休的人。
When researching this book, I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40.
好吧，但是一个人能挣多少钱需要退休吗？
OK, but how much money does a person need to retire?
我读过一些文章推荐 100 万美元作为退休后的好身材。
I've read articles recommending $1 million as a good figure for retirement.
虽然大多数理财规划师都会给出数字，但我我认为这没什么用，因为人们生活不同地区的生活成本也不同有不同的需求和愿望，为什么我建议人们以财务为目标独立。
While most financial planners do give numbers, I don't think that's useful, as people are living in different areas with different costs of living and have different needs and wants, which is why I suggest that people aim for financial independence.
投资收入大于每月支出。
Having investment income that's greater than monthly expenses.
我觉得这听起来很危险。
That sounds risky to me.
人们难道不应该留有额外的现金以备不时之需吗？
Shouldn't people have extra cash for emergencies?
很多人一生都在致力于他们因为害怕而讨厌的工作，所以我劝告人们去冒险。
Too many people spend their lives working on jobs they hate because they're afraid, so I counsel people to take risks.
退休不一定是永久的，如果人们需要，他们可以回到工作。
Retirement doesn't have to be permanent, and if people need to, they can go back to work.
但恢复并不总是那么容易经过长期缺勤后重返工作岗位。
But it's not always easy to get back into the workforce after an extended absence.
没错，但如果你跟上你的技能，你将对雇主具有吸引力。
True, but if you keep current with your skills, you will be attractive to employers.
也许吧，但谁能存够足够的钱呢？大多数人无法退休时，40 岁就退休60 岁？
Maybe, but how can anyone save enough to retire by 40 when most people can't retire at 60?
简单的。
Simple.
通过削减住房、食品和交通开支，投资你月收入的一半。
By cutting housing, food and transport expenses and investing half your monthly income.
这听起来不可能。
That sounds impossible.
我承认这很困难，但确实有效数千人。
I admit it's difficult, but it has worked for thousands.
